title: Certificates of Deposit: reversing a penalty booked at the wrong rate or the wrong number of days
content:
## Situation this policy governs

On a Certificates of Deposit certificate, an early withdrawal penalty is checked against the rate and the penalty days that the charter fixes for the term in which the withdrawal was taken. A penalty booked at any other rate or any other number of penalty days was assessed contrary to the charter, and it is reversed with the adjustment reason bank error.

The business result governed by this policy is the amount credited back to the certificate. The credit is booked with the tool described below, and it shows at once as a penalty reversal in the certificate's activity and as a higher principal balance.

## Tool: reverse_penalty_error_2ccc5de3

### What it does

The tool credits an early withdrawal penalty back to a certificate of deposit as a bank-error correction. It posts one penalty reversal entry on the certificate, dated today, that points to the penalty entry being reversed and carries the adjustment reason bank_error. The amount credited is added to the certificate's principal balance at once, so the owner sees the credit in the certificate's activity and a higher principal balance right away. Nothing else about the certificate changes.

### How it is invoked

reverse_penalty_error_2ccc5de3 is an internal tool that the agent must first unlock and then call; the agent performs it.

### Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| certificate_id | The certificate reference number of the certificate that carries the penalty, as returned by the certificate lookup for this customer | Identifier |
| source_item_id | The entry reference number of the early withdrawal penalty entry being credited back, as returned by the certificate activity lookup | Identifier |
| amount | The amount credited back to principal | USD, 2 decimal places, a positive number rounded half up to the cent |

### What it returns

A successful call returns a receipt, rendered as text, with:

- reversal_id: the entry reference number of the new penalty reversal entry;
- certificate_id: the certificate credited;
- source_item_id: the penalty entry it reverses;
- amount: the USD amount credited, to 2 decimal places;
- posted_date: today, as YYYY-MM-DD;
- principal_balance: the certificate's new principal in USD, to 2 decimal places.

A receipt carrying a reversal_id means the credit is posted.

## Contract questions

**Does the tool decide whether a penalty is wrong?**
No. It posts the reversal with the values supplied; the reversal decision is a matter of policy.

**Which reason does the entry carry?**
Always bank_error.

**Illustrative receipt (hypothetical values).** A call for a certificate with an amount of 57.13 returns a reversal_id, the same certificate_id and source_item_id, amount 57.13, today's posted_date, and a principal_balance 57.13 higher than before the call.
